About

Ground Floor

I run this project from a home office. The gear doing the work is two M5 Max MacBook Pros connected over Thunderbolt 5 RDMA — 256 GB of unified memory, 4 TB of storage, ~3 µs latency between nodes. The same hardware I write about on this site. None of it is theoretical.

Why this work

I kept seeing the same conversation repeat. A solo physician asks about AI documentation tools. The products people recommend — all of them excellent — require an internet connection, a vendor agreement, and some number of calls with a compliance consultant. The physician, who runs a single-provider practice with two staff and no IT department, quietly closes the browser tab.

The tools that exist for large health systems don't translate well to small practices. The tools built for small practices often handle the compliance question with a checkbox and a promise. There's a third option that almost nobody is covering in a systematic way: run the model locally, on hardware you already understand, and don't create a third-party data flow in the first place.

That's the gap Ground Floor is trying to close. Not with a product — this is an education project, not a company — but with clear documentation of what actually works.

The format

Each week I run a specific experiment: a specific model, on specific hardware, doing a specific task for a specific regulated industry. I document the setup, the results, the failure modes, and what someone would need to replicate it. The verdict answers the question most people actually have: is this worth my time?

The companion videos go on YouTube. The writeups live here. The discussion happens on LinkedIn. This site is the reference layer.

What I'm not

I'm not a lawyer, a compliance consultant, a physician, a financial advisor, or a licensed professional in any of the industries I write about. I'm someone who understands local LLM infrastructure and wants to make that knowledge accessible to people who don't have time to piece it together from technical papers and Discord servers.

Every experiment result is a technical finding. The compliance implications for your practice are a separate question that requires someone who knows your specific situation. The Scope & Disclaimers page says this more carefully.

The lab setup

Two M5 Max MacBook Pros connected over Thunderbolt 5 RDMA — 256 GB total unified memory, 4 TB storage, ~800 GB/s peak bandwidth between nodes. This cluster handles the full experiment range: from entry-tier simulations (deliberately constrained to 16 GB to match a base Mac mini) up to large-context multi-step workloads at 70B.

When an experiment is documented as "viable at entry level," the setup was deliberately throttled to that tier. The cluster gives room to test across the full hardware spectrum without buying multiple machines.

Contact

Best way to reach me is email: hello@groundfloor.local. I read everything. If you're a practitioner in a regulated industry who wants to share a use case, challenge a finding, or suggest an experiment — especially welcome. The experiments get better when they're grounded in real workflows.
